citeAs: Yue, X., Ni, Y., Zhang, K., Zheng, T., Liu, R., Zhang, G., Stevens, S., Jiang, D., Ren, W., Sun, Y., Wei, C., Yu, B., Yuan, R., Sun, R., Yin, M., Zheng, B., Yang, Z., Liu, Y., Huang, W., Sun, H., Su, Y., & Chen, W. (2024). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning, containing 11.5K multimodal questions.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, and categorized into four difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions where necessary. They were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations, avoid data from sites prohibiting redistribution, and select questions without immediately available answers.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
rai:dataCollection: Subjects were selected based on the commonality of visual inputs. Over 50 university students collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources.
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults'.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with design criteria, were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify and eliminate duplicate problems. Format and typo checking were performed to ensure adherence to a standardized format.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI is of societal importance due to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Not applicable to this benchmark dataset.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools were used for dataset creation.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Not explicitly stated how many annotations per item were collected.
